# Dusty v2.1.0 - Memory, the honest way
Dusty now frees memory too. Not with a "boost RAM" button that runs `purge` as root, but the way that actually gives memory back: by showing which apps are holding it and quitting the ones you are not using, after you say so.

**A Memory screen**

- **The real picture.** Memory in use, split the way Activity Monitor splits it (apps, system, compressed, cached files), swap, the last hour as a graph, and memory pressure, the one figure that says whether your Mac actually needs more.
- **Apps, not processes.** Every app's total counts all the processes working for it: Chrome's helpers, Safari's web pages, the tools a terminal started. That is exactly what quitting the app gives back.
- **Idle apps, already ticked.** Big apps you have not used for an hour are suggested. Dusty knows when you last used each app because it notices when you switch. Terminals, virtual machines, calls, and anything playing or recording sound are never suggested.
- **Free up, with a way back.** One tap quits the suggested apps after a confirmation that lists every app and its memory. They quit the way ⌘Q quits them, so anything with unsaved work asks first. For a few seconds afterwards, **Reopen** (or ⌘Z) brings them all back.
- **Leaks, caught.** An app that keeps growing (a browser open all week, a leaky Electron app) is flagged with how much it grew, and **Relaunch** gives that memory back without losing your place.

**Around it**

- Memory on the home screen, right under the disk, with its own **Free up** button whenever idle apps are sitting on memory. One tap and a confirmation, without opening anything else.
- An optional `RAM 72%` in the menu bar (Settings > Menu bar).
- A notification when memory pressure stays high, naming the apps holding the most. Once per episode, never twice in six hours, and it can be turned off in Settings > Memory.
- A **Get Memory Usage** Shortcuts action, and `dusty memory [--top N] [--json]` in the command line. Both only read.
- Everything new is translated into French, Spanish, and Russian.

**What it will not do**

Dusty never force quits, never kills a process, never runs `purge`, and never asks for root. Purging only drops the file cache, which macOS already hands to any app the moment it asks, so it just makes your Mac read those files from disk again. Nothing in the memory feature touches a file.

**Install**

```
brew install --cask yagcioglutoprak/tap/dusty
```

Or download `Dusty-2.1.0.dmg` below. It is signed and notarized, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning. If you already have Dusty, it updates itself.
